quote: You only live twice: / Once when you are born / And once when you look death in the face.
source: Ian Fleming, You Only Live Twice, the epigraph, printed as after Bashō (Jonathan Cape, 1964)

evidence.where: Full text of the novel in a digital copy (mural.uv.es PDF), read with pdftotext: the epigraph page prints the three lines with the credit After BASHO, Japanese poet, 1643-94; in chapter 11, Anatomy Class, Bond composes the verse for Tiger Tanaka, who says it has the wrong number of syllables. Not the Cape first edition itself
evidence.edition: Jonathan Cape, 1964 (text read in an unofficial digital copy)
evidence.locator: epigraph; composed by Bond in chapter 11, Anatomy Class

reason: The epigraph reads exactly as proposed, full stop included. It is Fleming's own verse: the novel has Bond write it in chapter 11 and Tiger calls it a failed haiku, so the Bashō credit is Fleming's joke and the card rightly credits Fleming. Fleming is at 0 of 3 and shipped check is clean; the Cape page itself was not opened.
